name: Match Group, Inc.
moat_justification: Tinder's unmatched local network liquidity and a portfolio of brands (Hinge growing direct revenue +22% in Q2 2026) give real scale and pricing power — revenue per payer +6% while payers fell — and the ROIC proxy has run 17-27% over the last five fiscal years on ~70-73% gross margins. But switching costs are near zero, users multi-home, Tinder payers are falling (-5% in Q2 2026) and Gen Z swipe fatigue is a structural headwind, so the network can erode from the edges.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 3.8%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.1x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 3.1x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (9.0%) vs bull-case tier C (14.6%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Quality cash machine, moat 6/10 — TTM owner's earnings $3.61/share and ROIC proxy ~23-27%, but at $45.21 it does not clear 15%: weighted IRR 11.2%, IV@15 $31.24; it clears 15% only below ~$31.
moat_for: Tinder's scale: the largest dating-app user pool gives local matching liquidity rivals cannot replicate quickly
Portfolio breadth — Hinge (+22% direct revenue, +17% payers in Q2 2026), Evergreen & Emerging niche brands, MG Asia — diversifies a single-app decline
Demonstrated pricing power: revenue per payer +6% YoY in Q2 2026 even as payers fell 6%
High returns on capital: ROIC proxy 22.9-26.7% in FY2023-25 (17.0% in the 2022 settlement year) with gross margins of ~70-73%
Trust & safety operations and brand recognition at global scale
moat_against: Tinder erosion: payers -5% and MAU declining in Q2 2026; total payers -6% YoY to 13.3M
Near-zero switching costs and routine multi-homing; network effects are local and can unravel market by market
Gen Z fatigue with swipe dating and substitution toward social apps, events and offline meeting
Focused rivals (Bumble, Grindr, niche and AI-companion apps) taking share of intentioned daters
App-store fee and regulatory pressure on the in-app purchase model
